76.name: Song of the Three Young Men

person.name: David
person.title: King of Judah, then of all Israel
person.tagline: Seven years in Hebron, thirty-three in Jerusalem.

capital.name: Jerusalem
capital.note: Hebron for the first seven years and six months, then Jerusalem, “the city of David”.

reign.text: Forty years: seven years and six months in Hebron over Judah, thirty-three in Jerusalem over all Israel and Judah (2 Samuel 5:4–5). 1 Kings 2:11 and 1 Chronicles 29:27 give the Hebron years as seven.

verdict.text: David did that which was right in the eyes of the LORD, and turned not aside from any thing that he commanded him all the days of his life, save only in the matter of Uriah the Hittite

death.text: He gave Solomon his last charge and “slept with his fathers”.

burial.text: was buried in the city of David

death.text: “he died in a good old age, full of days, riches, and honour”, and Solomon reigned in his place.

sourcesCited.text: the acts of David the king, first and last, behold, they are written in the book of Samuel the seer, and in the book of Nathan the prophet, and in the book of Gad the seer

identifications.text: The site's family data lists “Nahash” as one of David's parents. That is STEP Bible's reading of 2 Samuel 17:25, where Abigail, sister of Zeruiah, is called “the daughter of Nahash”; Chronicles calls Zeruiah and Abigail David's sisters. Scripture names Jesse as David's father and does not name his mother. This page does not rely on the Nahash link.

person.brief: Anointed king of Israel, ancestor of Jesus Christ

reign.text: Forty years, by Acts 13:21. In 1 Samuel 13:1, where the age and length should stand, the Hebrew numbers are incomplete.

death.text: Badly wounded by the archers on mount Gilboa, Saul fell on his own sword. Three of his sons died the same day.

reign.text: “reigned two years” (2 Samuel 2:10), while David was king in Hebron over Judah for seven years and six months.

death.text: Two of his own captains, Rechab and Baanah, killed him on his bed at noon and took his head to David at Hebron.

reign.text: “forty years” in Jerusalem over all Israel (1 Kings 11:42; 2 Chronicles 9:30).

groupIntro.text: The united kingdom is the time when one king ruled all the tribes: Saul, then David, then Solomon. Ish-bosheth, Saul's son, held the northern tribes for two years while David reigned over Judah in Hebron.

Its story is told twice: in 1–2 Samuel and 1 Kings 1–11, and again in 1 Chronicles 10–29 and 2 Chronicles 1–9. Chronicles leaves out most of Saul's reign, all of Ish-bosheth's, and many of David's and Solomon's troubles, and adds David's preparations for the temple. These pages show the two accounts side by side and do not merge them.
It ended as Ahijah had said: ten tribes made Jeroboam king, and only Judah followed the house of David.

Scripture gives reign lengths, not BC years. The main dates here follow Thiele's chronology as worked out for this period by McFall (2010) and Young (2003); the traditional dates of Ussher (1658) and the dates that follow from Albright's 922 BC are shown beside them.

story.short: The youngest son of Jesse of Bethlehem, a shepherd anointed by Samuel, who killed Goliath, fled from Saul, reigned forty years, and was called "the sweet psalmist of Israel".

paragraphs.text: David was the son of Jesse, an Ephrathite of Beth-lehem-judah, and great-grandson of Boaz and Ruth. Samuel says Jesse had eight sons and that David was the youngest; Chronicles names seven, with David the seventh, and gives him two sisters, Zeruiah and Abigail. Scripture never names his mother. He was keeping the sheep when Samuel came and anointed him among his brothers: "he was ruddy, and withal of a beautiful countenance", and from that day the Spirit of the LORD came upon him.

He came to Saul's court as a harp player and armourbearer. Sent to bring food to his brothers in the army, he went out against the Philistine champion Goliath "in the name of the LORD of hosts" and killed him with a sling and a stone. Saul's son Jonathan "loved him as his own soul", and the two made a covenant. David married Saul's daughter Michal, and when Saul sent men to kill him, she let him down through a window.

Then he lived as a fugitive from Saul. At the cave of Adullam his brothers and his father's house joined him, with about four hundred men, and he left his father and mother with the king of Moab. Twice he had Saul in his power and would not harm "the LORD's anointed". He married Abigail, the widow of Nabal, and Ahinoam of Jezreel, while Saul gave Michal to another man. When Saul and Jonathan died, he lamented, "How are the mighty fallen!"

David was thirty when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years; the reign is told on his page as a ruler. When the ark came into Jerusalem he danced before the LORD with all his might, and Michal despised him; she had no child to the day of her death. He sought out Jonathan's lame son Mephibosheth and had him eat at the king's table. Sons were born to him at Hebron and at Jerusalem.

He took Bath-sheba, the wife of Uriah, and had Uriah killed in battle. The prophet Nathan told him, "Thou art the man", and David said, "I have sinned against the LORD." Their first child died; their next son was Solomon. Trouble followed in his house: his son Amnon forced Absalom's sister Tamar, Absalom had Amnon killed, and later Absalom rose against his father and was killed in the battle that followed. David wept, "O my son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom! would God I had died for thee".

In old age, "old and stricken in years", David named Solomon king when Adonijah tried to take the throne. He charged Solomon, "be thou strong therefore, and shew thyself a man", then died and was buried in the city of David. His last words call him "the sweet psalmist of Israel". Chronicles says he "died in a good old age, full of days, riches, and honour", and Acts recalls God's words about him: "a man after mine own heart".

accession.text: Samuel anointed David, Jesse's youngest son, at Bethlehem “in the midst of his brethren”, while Saul still reigned.
After Saul's death David asked the LORD where to go, went up to Hebron, and “the men of Judah came, and there they anointed David king over the house of Judah”.
After Abner and Ish-bosheth were dead, the tribes came to Hebron; David “made a league with them”, and “they anointed David king over Israel”.
Chronicles tells only this last anointing, “according to the word of the LORD by Samuel”, and lists the armed men of every tribe who came to Hebron “to make David king over all Israel”.
So 1–2 Samuel record three anointings: by Samuel at Bethlehem, by Judah at Hebron, and by Israel's elders at Hebron.

claim.text: “there they anointed David king over the house of Judah.”

events.label: War with the house of Saul

claim.text: Joab beat Abner at the pool of Gibeon, and the long war followed.
The elders of Israel anointed him king over Israel at Hebron after seven years and six months there.
David took “the strong hold of Zion”, lived in the fort, called it “the city of David”, and built round about from Millo.

events.label: Philistines beaten in the valley of Rephaim

claim.text: Twice the Philistines came up; David beat them at Baal-perazim and then “from Geba until thou come to Gazer”.
Hiram king of Tyre sent messengers, cedar trees, carpenters and masons, “and they built David an house”.
Bringing the ark from Baale of Judah on a new cart, Uzzah took hold of it and died. The ark stayed three months with Obed-edom.
David brought the ark into the city of David with sacrifices, dancing “with all his might”, and set it in the tent he had pitched. Michal despised him.
David wanted to build a house for the ark. Through Nathan the LORD said that David's son would build it, and that David's house, kingdom and throne would be “established for ever”.
David took Metheg-ammah from the Philistines and made Moab his servants, bringing gifts.
David struck Hadadezer of Zobah “as he went to recover his border at the river Euphrates”, killed 22,000 Syrians of Damascus who came to help, and put garrisons in Damascus.
Toi, Hadadezer's enemy, sent his son Joram with vessels of silver, gold and brass, which David dedicated to the LORD.
“all they of Edom became David's servants.”
For Jonathan's sake David restored Saul's land to Jonathan's lame son and had him eat at the king's table.
Hanun of Ammon shamed David's messengers and hired Syrians. Joab and Abishai beat both, and David beat Hadarezer's Syrians at Helam.

While Joab besieged Rabbah, David lay with Bathsheba, Uriah's wife, then had Uriah put “in the forefront of the hottest battle”, where he was killed. “But the thing that David had done displeased the LORD.”
Nathan's parable of the ewe lamb, the LORD's sentence, and David's confession. The child died.
Bathsheba bore Solomon; “the LORD loved him”, and Nathan named him Jedidiah.
David took Rabbah, the royal city of Ammon, and the crown of its king.
Amnon forced his half-sister Tamar. Two years later Absalom had him killed and fled to Geshur for three years.
Absalom “stole the hearts of the men of Israel”, had himself proclaimed king in Hebron, and drew Ahithophel to his side.

events.label: Flight over the mount of Olives

claim.text: David left Jerusalem and went up the ascent of the mount of Olives weeping, barefoot. At Bahurim Shimei cursed him.
David's men beat Israel in the wood of Ephraim. Absalom was caught by his head in an oak, and Joab killed him. David wept: “O my son Absalom”.

events.label: Return, and Judah and Israel quarrel

claim.text: Judah brought the king back over the Jordan; the men of Israel complained that Judah had “stolen thee away”.

Sheba blew a trumpet: “We have no part in David”. Israel followed him; Judah stayed with David. Joab killed Amasa, besieged Sheba in Abel of Beth-maachah, and the city threw Sheba's head over the wall.

Three years of famine were laid to Saul's killing of Gibeonites. David handed seven of Saul's descendants to the Gibeonites, spared Mephibosheth, and buried Saul's and Jonathan's bones in Kish's tomb.
In four battles David's men killed four men “born to the giant in Gath”. David “waxed faint”, and his men swore he would go out to battle no more.
David's song of deliverance, and the “last words” of “the sweet psalmist of Israel”.
David had Joab number Israel and Judah; it took nine months and twenty days.
Offered famine, flight or pestilence, David chose to fall “into the hand of the LORD”. Seventy thousand died, and the angel stopped by the threshingfloor of Araunah.
At Gad's word David bought the threshingfloor and built an altar, “and the plague was stayed from Israel”. Chronicles adds that David said, “This is the house of the LORD God”.
Chronicles alone tells how David gathered gold, silver, brass, iron, timber and stone, ordered the Levites, priests, singers and gatekeepers, and gave Solomon the pattern of the house.
When David was old, Adonijah declared himself king. At Nathan's and Bathsheba's urging David had Solomon anointed at Gihon.
David charged Solomon to keep the LORD's ways, and died.

verdictNotes.text: Kings' verdict names its one exception: “save only in the matter of Uriah the Hittite”.
Nathan gave him the LORD's sentence for that act: “the sword shall never depart from thine house”. David answered, “I have sinned against the LORD”.
After the census he said, “I have sinned greatly in that I have done”.
Kings measures later kings by him: Solomon's heart “was not perfect with the LORD his God, as was the heart of David his father”.
Chronicles gives the reason David might not build the temple: “Thou hast shed blood abundantly, and hast made great wars”.
In Acts, Paul quotes God's word about him: “I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after mine own heart”.

worship.text: David brought the ark to Jerusalem and set it in a tent he had pitched.
Zadok and Ahimelech son of Abiathar were the priests.
Chronicles describes the Levites' music before the ark and their courses, set up by David; a later king followed “the commandment of David, and of Gad the king's seer, and Nathan the prophet”.
He built an altar on Araunah's threshingfloor; Chronicles says the LORD answered “from heaven by fire”.
Scripture calls him “the sweet psalmist of Israel”.

building.text: He built “round about from Millo and inward” in the city of David.
Hiram's carpenters and masons built his house of cedar.
He was not allowed to build the temple; his son would build it.
Chronicles counts his stores for it: “an hundred thousand talents of gold, and a thousand thousand talents of silver”.

alliances.text: Hiram of Tyre, who “was ever a lover of David”.
Toi of Hamath sent gifts after David beat Hadadezer.
Nahash of Ammon had shown him kindness.
He married Maacah, daughter of Talmai king of Geshur, Absalom's mother.
Before he reigned he had served Achish of Gath, who gave him Ziklag.
Peoples paid him tribute: Moab, Syria of Damascus, Edom.

people.text: “David executed judgment and justice unto all his people.”
His officers: Joab over the host, Jehoshaphat recorder, Seraiah scribe (Sheva in the later list), Benaiah over the Cherethites and Pelethites, Adoram over the tribute.
The census counted 800,000 men of Israel and 500,000 of Judah.
Judah and Israel were rivals within his kingdom: “We have ten parts in the king”, said Israel; Sheba's cry “We have no part in David” returned word for word at the division.

claim.text: Samuel anointed David at Bethlehem and sheltered him at Naioth in Ramah when he fled from Saul.

quote.text: man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart

claim.text: Gad, “David's seer”, told him to leave the hold for Judah, brought the LORD's three choices after the census, and told him to build the altar on Araunah's threshingfloor. Chronicles names his book as a source.

quote.text: Shall seven years of famine come unto thee in thy land

claim.text: Nathan brought the promise of David's house, confronted him over Uriah, named Solomon Jedidiah, and with Bathsheba secured Solomon's anointing. Chronicles names his book as a source.
David served Achish before he reigned, then beat the Philistines in the valley of Rephaim and took Metheg-ammah; late in his reign came the wars with the giants of Gath.

rulers.name: Rezon
rulers.note: Fled from Hadadezer and later reigned in Damascus (1 Kgs 11:23–24).

claim.text: David beat Hadadezer and the Syrians of Damascus, put garrisons in Damascus, and beat them again at Helam.
Toi greeted David's victory over Hadadezer with gifts.
Friendly under Nahash; at war under his son Hanun until Rabbah fell. In Absalom's revolt Shobi son of Nahash brought David supplies.
Both became David's servants. Kings adds that Joab spent six months in Edom “until he had cut off every male”, and that the young prince Hadad fled to Egypt.
Hiram supplied cedar and craftsmen for David's house.
David's father-in-law; Absalom fled to him after killing Amnon.
Before he reigned David recovered everything the Amalekites took from Ziklag; their spoil is among the gifts he dedicated.

An Aramaic victory stele found at Tel Dan has a king of Aram speak of the “king of Israel” and of “bytdwd”, which its editors Biran and Naveh read as “house of David”, a name for Judah's royal line. It was written more than a century after David and does not describe him.

outside.name: Nicolaus of Damascus, quoted by Josephus (Antiquities 7.5.2)
outside.date: first century BC; quoted about AD 93

claim.text: Josephus quotes Nicolaus of Damascus as writing that a king of Damascus named Hadad “made war against David, the king of Judea”, and was beaten “in the last battle at Euphrates”. Nicolaus wrote about nine centuries after David, and his source is not known.
None of the sources used for this page cites an inscription from David's own lifetime that names him. The Tel Dan stele, above, is more than a century later.

twoAccounts.topic: Who moved David to number the people

first.text: 2 Samuel: “the anger of the LORD was kindled against Israel, and he moved David against them”.

second.text: 1 Chronicles: “Satan stood up against Israel, and provoked David to number Israel”.

first.text: 2 Samuel: 800,000 men of Israel and 500,000 of Judah.

second.text: 1 Chronicles: 1,100,000 of Israel and 470,000 of Judah.

twoAccounts.topic: The price of the threshingfloor, and its owner

first.text: 2 Samuel: Araunah's threshingfloor and oxen for “fifty shekels of silver”.

second.text: 1 Chronicles: Ornan's place for “six hundred shekels of gold by weight”.

first.text: 2 Samuel: Elhanan son of Jaare-oregim “slew the brother of Goliath the Gittite”. In the KJV “the brother of” is printed as supplied words; the Hebrew reads that Elhanan slew Goliath.

second.text: 1 Chronicles: “Elhanan the son of Jair slew Lahmi the brother of Goliath the Gittite”.

first.text: 2 Samuel: “a thousand chariots, and seven hundred horsemen”.

second.text: 1 Chronicles: “a thousand chariots, and seven thousand horsemen”.

twoAccounts.topic: The Syrians killed at the end of the Ammonite war

first.text: 2 Samuel: “the men of seven hundred chariots of the Syrians, and forty thousand horsemen”.

second.text: 1 Chronicles: “seven thousand men which fought in chariots, and forty thousand footmen”.

first.text: 2 Samuel: David struck “the Syrians in the valley of salt, being eighteen thousand men”.

second.text: 1 Chronicles: “Abishai the son of Zeruiah slew of the Edomites in the valley of salt eighteen thousand”.

first.text: 2 Samuel: David “took Metheg-ammah out of the hand of the Philistines”.

second.text: 1 Chronicles: he “took Gath and her towns out of the hand of the Philistines”.

twoAccounts.topic: The chief of the mighty men

first.text: 2 Samuel: “Adino the Eznite”, who lifted his spear “against eight hundred, whom he slew at one time”.

second.text: 1 Chronicles: “Jashobeam, an Hachmonite”, who lifted his spear “against three hundred slain by him at one time”.

first.text: 2 Samuel tells of the war with Saul's house while David was in Hebron, his kindness to Mephibosheth, Bathsheba and Uriah, Nathan's rebuke, Amnon and Tamar, Absalom's revolt, Sheba's rising and the hanging of Saul's descendants.

second.text: 1 Chronicles says that “David tarried at Jerusalem” while Joab besieged Rabbah, then tells the city's fall, and moves on to the Philistine wars. None of those stories is told; for the Hebron years it gives only the length, “seven years and six months”.

first.text: 1 Kings: Adonijah declared himself king; Nathan and Bathsheba went to David; Zadok and Nathan anointed Solomon at Gihon.

second.text: 1 Chronicles: David “made Solomon his son king over Israel”, and later “they made Solomon the son of David king the second time”, with all David's sons submitting. Adonijah is not mentioned.

questions.question: Who killed Goliath: David or Elhanan? (Views as Keil reports them, 1866.)

views.label: Chronicles keeps the original reading
views.holders: Piscator, Clericus, Michaelis, Movers and Thenius, and Keil himself (tr. 1866)

argument.text: The two verses differ by a few Hebrew letters. Keil held that 2 Samuel was miscopied from a text like Chronicles', so Elhanan killed Goliath's brother Lahmi; David killed Goliath.

views.label: Samuel keeps the original reading
views.holders: Bertheau and Böttcher, as reported by Keil (1866)

argument.text: They held that Chronicles altered a reading that said Elhanan killed a giant named Goliath, out of offence at the clash with 1 Samuel 17.

questions.question: Who moved David to take the census?

views.label: Both: the LORD moved David, through Satan as tempter

argument.text: Keil takes the LORD as the one who moved David, in anger at Israel's guilt, which he finds in the revolts of Absalom and Sheba; Chronicles names Satan as the tempter through whom the LORD led David to number the people.
Wellhausen treated 1 Chronicles 21 as a copy of 2 Samuel 24 with “improving touches”, of which Satan in place of the LORD's anger is one.

questions.question: Absalom's revolt came “after forty years” (2 Samuel 15:7). Forty years from what?

argument.text: Josephus gives “four years” after Absalom's reconciliation with his father. Whiston's note calls this one of the best corrections Josephus offers, and cites the copy of the Greek used by the Armenian translation.

views.label: Forty years from Samuel's anointing of David

argument.text: Ussher dated the revolt forty years after Samuel anointed David. McFall argues the same way, noting that the Hebrew and nearly all Greek manuscripts read forty.

questions.question: When did Hiram of Tyre build David's house?

views.label: A different, earlier Hiram
views.holders: Thenius and Ewald, as reported by Keil (1866)

argument.text: Josephus's Tyrian figures seem to start Hiram's reign late in David's life, so Thenius suggested that Hiram's father Abibal is meant in David's story, and Ewald that Abibal's own father was also called Hiram.

views.label: Samuel's order is by topic, not date

argument.text: 2 Samuel 5 groups the building of Jerusalem with its capture, so Hiram's help may come years later.

views.label: Josephus's dating is his own calculation

argument.text: Keil notes that Scripture makes the same Hiram a friend of both kings, and argues that the temple-in-Hiram's-twelfth-year figure is Josephus's own reckoning, not Menander's, so Hiram may have reigned longer.

questions.question: Does the Tel Dan stele name the house of David?

views.label: Yes: “house of David”, the dynasty of Judah

argument.text: The excavators read the word as “house of David”, a name for the kingdom of Judah by its founding king.
Davies questioned whether the stele mentions David at all, holding that such readings should be tested before they are treated as fact.

notSaid: Scripture does not name David's mother.
Scripture does not give his age at his first anointing or when he fought Goliath.
Apart from his first year in Hebron, his move to all Israel after seven and a half years, and his death in his fortieth year, Scripture does not say in which year of his reign most events happened.
Scripture does not say how long Absalom's revolt lasted.
No outside record from David's own lifetime names him.

dates.label: Scripture's numbers
dates.note: Thirty years old at accession; seven years and six months in Hebron; thirty-three years in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 5:4–5).

dates.label: McFall (2010), building on Thiele
dates.note: King of Judah at Hebron 1010 BC; of all Israel 1003 BC; died 970 BC (McFall). Young (2003) puts Solomon's first official year in 972 or 971 BC, overlapping David's last.

dates.label: Counted back from Albright's 922 BC
dates.note: Albright dated the division of the kingdom to 922 BC. Scripture's forty years for Solomon then put David's death about 962 BC. Albright's own figure for David's accession was not checked for this page.

dates.label: Traditional (Ussher, 1658)
dates.note: King in Hebron 1055 BC; over all Israel 1048 BC; Jerusalem taken 1047 BC; Solomon made king 1015 BC. Ussher has David live about six months more and die in 1014 BC.

kish-1sa-9-1.name: Kish
kish-1sa-9-1.brief: Father of Saul, the first king of Israel
kish-1sa-9-1.short: Kish was a Benjamite, the father of Saul, who was anointed by Samuel as the first king of Israel.

saul-1sa-9-2.name: Saul
saul-1sa-9-2.brief: First king of Israel, anointed by Samuel
saul-1sa-9-2.short: Saul was the first king of Israel, anointed by the prophet Samuel, who initially followed God but later disobeyed and was rejected as king.
saul-1sa-9-2.story: A tall young Benjamite, son of Kish, anointed as Israel's first king, who lost God's favour, turned against David, and died on mount Gilboa.

abner-1sa-14-50.name: Abner
abner-1sa-14-50.brief: Saul's cousin and commander of his army
abner-1sa-14-50.short: Abner, the son of Ner, was King Saul's cousin and the commander of his army; he later supported Saul's son Ish-bosheth as king before defecting to David.
abner-1sa-14-50.story: The son of Ner and captain of Saul's host, who made Ish-bosheth king, then turned to David, and was killed by Joab in the gate of Hebron.

rizpah-2sa-3-7.name: Rizpah
rizpah-2sa-3-7.brief: Concubine of Saul; mother of Armoni and Mephibosheth
rizpah-2sa-3-7.short: Rizpah was a concubine of King Saul and the mother of Armoni and Mephibosheth, who were executed by the Gibeonites.

jonathan-1sa-13-2.name: Jonathan
jonathan-1sa-13-2.brief: Eldest son of King Saul and friend of David
jonathan-1sa-13-2.short: Jonathan, the eldest son of King Saul, was a valiant warrior and a close friend of David, ultimately dying in battle alongside his father.
jonathan-1sa-13-2.story: Saul's son, a warrior who attacked a Philistine garrison with only his armourbearer, loved David as his own soul, and died with his father on mount Gilboa.

abinadab-1sa-14-49.name: Abinadab
abinadab-1sa-14-49.brief: Son of King Saul, killed in battle
abinadab-1sa-14-49.short: Abinadab, also known as Ishvi, was one of the sons of King Saul who died alongside his father and brothers in battle against the Philistines at Mount Gilboa.

malchi-shua-1sa-14-49.name: Malchi-shua
malchi-shua-1sa-14-49.brief: Son of King Saul, killed in battle against the Philistines.
malchi-shua-1sa-14-49.short: Malchi-shua, a son of King Saul, was killed in battle against the Philistines.

ish-bosheth-2sa-2-8.name: Ish-bosheth
ish-bosheth-2sa-2-8.brief: Son of Saul, king over Israel.
ish-bosheth-2sa-2-8.short: Ish-bosheth (also called Eshbaal), Saul's son, was made king over Israel by Abner but was ultimately assassinated, leading to David's rule over all Israel.
ish-bosheth-2sa-2-8.story: Saul's son, made king over Israel by Abner for two years while Judah followed David, and murdered in his bed by two of his captains.

merab-1sa-14-49.name: Merab
merab-1sa-14-49.short: Merab, the eldest daughter of King Saul, was promised to David but given to Adriel.

michal-1sa-14-49.name: Michal
michal-1sa-14-49.brief: Daughter of Saul; wife of David.
michal-1sa-14-49.short: Michal, the younger daughter of King Saul, became David's wife and helped him escape from Saul's attempts to kill him.

mephibosheth-2sa-4-4.name: Mephibosheth
mephibosheth-2sa-4-4.brief: Son of Jonathan and grandson of King Saul.
mephibosheth-2sa-4-4.short: Mephibosheth, also called Merib-baal, was the son of Jonathan and grandson of King Saul.

seven-of-saul.name: Seven of Saul's sons
seven-of-saul.brief: “the two sons of Rizpah … Armoni and Mephibosheth; and the five sons of Michal the daughter of Saul, whom she brought up for Adriel” (2 Samuel 21:8, KJV). Handed to the Gibeonites; “they fell all seven together” (21:9).

palti-1sa-25-44.name: Palti
palti-1sa-25-44.short: Palti (Paltiel), son of Laish, was Michal's husband from Gallim before she was taken back by David.

boaz-rut-2-1.name: Boaz
boaz-rut-2-1.brief: Kinsman-redeemer who married Ruth, ancestor of David and Jesus
boaz-rut-2-1.short: Boaz, a wealthy Bethlehemite, married Ruth and became an ancestor of King David and Jesus Christ.

ruth-rut-1-4.name: Ruth
ruth-rut-1-4.brief: Moabite woman, ancestor of David and Jesus
ruth-rut-1-4.short: Ruth was a Moabite woman who married Boaz and became an ancestor of King David and Jesus Christ.

obed-rut-4-17.name: Obed
obed-rut-4-17.short: Obed was the son of Boaz and Ruth, and the grandfather of King David.

jesse-rut-4-17.name: Jesse
jesse-rut-4-17.short: Jesse was the father of King David and an ancestor of Jesus Christ.
jesse-rut-4-17.story: A Beth-lehemite, grandson of Boaz and Ruth, whose youngest son David was anointed by Samuel; Scripture often calls David simply the son of Jesse.

eliab-1sa-16-6.name: Eliab
eliab-1sa-16-6.short: Eliab was the eldest brother of King David and the son of Jesse.

abinadab-1sa-16-8.name: Abinadab
abinadab-1sa-16-8.brief: Son of Jesse, brother of David
abinadab-1sa-16-8.short: Abinadab was one of the sons of Jesse and an older brother of King David, but he was not chosen to be anointed as king by Samuel.

shimeah-1sa-16-9.name: Shimeah
shimeah-1sa-16-9.brief: Brother of David; father of Jonadab (or 'Jonathan').
shimeah-1sa-16-9.short: Shimeah (also known as Shimei, Shammah, or Shimea) was a brother of King David and the father of Jonadab (or 'Jonathan').

nethanel-1ch-2-14.name: Nethanel
nethanel-1ch-2-14.short: Nethanel was a son of Jesse and brother of King David.

raddai-1ch-2-14.name: Raddai
raddai-1ch-2-14.brief: One of David's brothers, son of Jesse
raddai-1ch-2-14.short: Raddai was one of David's brothers, a son of Jesse.

ozem-1ch-2-15.name: Ozem
ozem-1ch-2-15.short: Ozem was one of David's brothers, a son of Jesse.

david-rut-4-17.name: David
david-rut-4-17.brief: Anointed king of Israel, ancestor of Jesus Christ
david-rut-4-17.short: David, son of Jesse, was the anointed king of Israel, a man after God's own heart, and an ancestor of Jesus Christ.
david-rut-4-17.story: The youngest son of Jesse of Bethlehem, a shepherd anointed by Samuel, who killed Goliath, fled from Saul, reigned forty years, and was called "the sweet psalmist of Israel".

zeruiah-1sa-26-6.name: Zeruiah
zeruiah-1sa-26-6.brief: Sister of David; mother of Joab, Abishai, and Asahel
zeruiah-1sa-26-6.short: Zeruiah, David's sister, was the mother of Joab, Abishai, and Asahel, who were among David's mighty men and military leaders.
zeruiah-1sa-26-6.story: The mother of Joab, Abishai and Asahel, named almost only through her sons; Chronicles lists her as a sister of David and his brothers.

abigail-2sa-17-25.name: Abigail
abigail-2sa-17-25.brief: Sister of David; mother of Amasa
abigail-2sa-17-25.short: Abigail, David's sister, was the mother of Amasa, who became the commander of Absalom's army.

joab-1sa-26-6.name: Joab
joab-1sa-26-6.brief: Son of Zeruiah, commander of David's army
joab-1sa-26-6.short: Joab, David's nephew and commander of his army, was a key figure in David's reign, known for his military prowess and loyalty.
joab-1sa-26-6.story: A son of Zeruiah and captain of David's host, who killed Abner and Amasa, struck Absalom with darts, and was put to death after fleeing to the altar.

abishai-1sa-26-6.name: Abishai
abishai-1sa-26-6.brief: David's nephew, one of his mighty men and commanders
abishai-1sa-26-6.short: Abishai, the son of Zeruiah and nephew of David, was a loyal commander and one of David's mighty men, known for his bravery and military prowess.

asahel-2sa-2-18.name: Asahel
asahel-2sa-2-18.brief: Son of Zeruiah, brother of Joab, killed by Abner
asahel-2sa-2-18.short: Asahel, son of Zeruiah and brother of Joab, was a fast runner killed by Abner during a battle (2Sam 2; 3:27, 30; 23:24; 1Ch.2.16; 11:26; 27:7).

amasa-2sa-17-25.name: Amasa
amasa-2sa-17-25.brief: Military commander, son of Abigail (David's sister), killed by Joab
amasa-2sa-17-25.short: Amasa, the son of Jether and Abigail (David's sister), was a military commander who served under Absalom and later David, but was killed by Joab.

jonadab-2sa-13-3.name: Jonadab
jonadab-2sa-13-3.brief: Nephew of David, friend and advisor to Amnon
jonadab-2sa-13-3.short: Jonadab, also known as Jonathan, was the son of David's brother Shimeah and a friend and advisor to Amnon, David's eldest son.

ahinoam-1sa-25-43.name: Ahinoam
ahinoam-1sa-25-43.brief: Wife of David, from Jezreel; mother of Amnon
ahinoam-1sa-25-43.short: Ahinoam of Jezreel was one of David's wives and the mother of his firstborn son, Amnon.

abigail-1sa-25-3.name: Abigail
abigail-1sa-25-3.brief: Wife of Nabal, later married David
abigail-1sa-25-3.short: Abigail, initially the wife of Nabal, became one of David's wives after Nabal's death and bore him a son named Chileab.

maacah-2sa-3-3.name: Maacah
maacah-2sa-3-3.brief: Daughter of Talmai; wife of David; mother of Absalom
maacah-2sa-3-3.short: Maacah, the daughter of King Talmai of Geshur, was one of David's wives and the mother of Absalom.

haggith-2sa-3-4.name: Haggith
haggith-2sa-3-4.brief: One of David's wives; mother of Adonijah.
haggith-2sa-3-4.short: Haggith was one of King David's wives and the mother of Adonijah, who attempted to claim the throne.

abital-2sa-3-4.name: Abital
abital-2sa-3-4.brief: One of David's wives; mother of Shephatiah
abital-2sa-3-4.short: Abital was one of King David's wives and the mother of his son Shephatiah.

eglah-2sa-3-5.name: Eglah
eglah-2sa-3-5.brief: David's wife and mother of Ithream
eglah-2sa-3-5.short: Eglah was one of David's wives and the mother of his son Ithream, born in Hebron.

bathsheba-2sa-11-3.name: Bathsheba
bathsheba-2sa-11-3.brief: Wife of Uriah, later married David and bore Solomon.
bathsheba-2sa-11-3.short: Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah, later became David's wife and the mother of Solomon.

jerusalem-wives-2sa-5-13.name: Jerusalem wives
jerusalem-wives-2sa-5-13.short: The unnamed wives David took in Jerusalem, who bore him more sons and daughters.

amnon-2sa-3-2.name: Amnon
amnon-2sa-3-2.brief: David's firstborn son, killed by Absalom
amnon-2sa-3-2.short: Amnon, David's firstborn son, raped his half-sister Tamar and was later killed by her brother Absalom.

chileab-2sa-3-3.name: Chileab
chileab-2sa-3-3.brief: Son of David and Abigail the Carmelitess
chileab-2sa-3-3.short: Chileab, also known as Daniel, was David's son by Abigail the Carmelitess.

absalom-2sa-3-3.name: Absalom
absalom-2sa-3-3.brief: David's rebellious son who tried to usurp the throne.
absalom-2sa-3-3.short: Absalom was David's third son who led a revolt against his father's reign.
absalom-2sa-3-3.story: David's third son, born at Hebron to Maacah of Geshur, who had his brother Amnon killed, rose against his father, and was slain in the wood of Ephraim.

tamar-2sa-13-1.name: Tamar
tamar-2sa-13-1.brief: David's daughter, raped by her half-brother Amnon
tamar-2sa-13-1.short: Tamar was David's daughter who was raped by her half-brother Amnon, leading to tragic consequences.

adonijah-2sa-3-4.name: Adonijah
adonijah-2sa-3-4.brief: Son of David who attempted to seize the throne
adonijah-2sa-3-4.short: Adonijah, the fourth son of David, declared himself king when David was old, but Solomon was chosen to succeed David instead, and Adonijah was later put to death for his rebellious actions.

shephatiah-2sa-3-4.name: Shephatiah
shephatiah-2sa-3-4.short: Shephatiah, the fifth son of David, born to him and his wife Abital in Hebron.

ithream-2sa-3-5.name: Ithream
ithream-2sa-3-5.brief: Son of David, born in Hebron to Eglah.
ithream-2sa-3-5.short: Ithream was a son of David, born to him in Hebron by his wife Eglah.

bathsheba-first-son.name: The child
bathsheba-first-son.brief: Bath-sheba “bare him a son” (2 Samuel 11:27); “on the seventh day … the child died” (12:18). He is not named.

shammua-2sa-5-14.name: Shammua
shammua-2sa-5-14.brief: Son of David born in Jerusalem
shammua-2sa-5-14.short: Shammua (or Shimea) was one of the sons of David born to him in Jerusalem.

shobab-2sa-5-14.name: Shobab
shobab-2sa-5-14.brief: Son of David and Bathsheba, born in Jerusalem.
shobab-2sa-5-14.short: Shobab was a son of David and Bathsheba, born to them in Jerusalem.

nathan-2sa-5-14.name: Nathan
nathan-2sa-5-14.brief: Son of David and Bathsheba, ancestor of Jesus.
nathan-2sa-5-14.short: Nathan, a son of David and Bathsheba, is mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus Christ.

solomon-2sa-5-14.name: Solomon
solomon-2sa-5-14.brief: Son of David, king of Israel, known for his wisdom.
solomon-2sa-5-14.short: Solomon, also called Jedidiah, was the son of David and Bathsheba who succeeded his father as king of Israel and was renowned for his wisdom, wealth, and the construction of the First Temple in Jerusalem.
solomon-2sa-5-14.story: David and Bath-sheba's son, loved by the LORD, who asked for wisdom, built the temple, and in old age was turned aside by his many wives.

ibhar-2sa-5-15.name: Ibhar
ibhar-2sa-5-15.brief: One of King David's sons born in Jerusalem.
ibhar-2sa-5-15.short: Ibhar was one of the sons born to David in Jerusalem, as recorded in 2 Samuel and 1 Chronicles.

elishua-2sa-5-15.name: Elishua
elishua-2sa-5-15.brief: A son of David born in Jerusalem.
elishua-2sa-5-15.short: Elishua, also known as Elishama, was a son of David born to him in Jerusalem.

elpelet-1ch-3-6.name: Elpelet
elpelet-1ch-3-6.brief: A son of David born in Jerusalem.
elpelet-1ch-3-6.short: Elpelet, also known as Eliphelet, was a son of David born in Jerusalem.

nogah-1ch-3-7.name: Nogah
nogah-1ch-3-7.short: Nogah was one of King David's sons born in Jerusalem.

nepheg-2sa-5-15.name: Nepheg
nepheg-2sa-5-15.brief: Son of King David, born in Jerusalem.
nepheg-2sa-5-15.short: Nepheg was one of the sons of King David, born to him in Jerusalem.

japhia-2sa-5-15.name: Japhia
japhia-2sa-5-15.brief: Son of David, born in Jerusalem
japhia-2sa-5-15.short: Japhia was one of King David's sons, born to him in Jerusalem.

elishama-2sa-5-16.name: Elishama
elishama-2sa-5-16.brief: A son of King David born in Jerusalem.
elishama-2sa-5-16.short: Elishama was a son of King David born to him in Jerusalem.

eliada-2sa-5-16.name: Eliada
eliada-2sa-5-16.brief: Son of David born in Jerusalem
eliada-2sa-5-16.short: Eliada, also known as Beeliada, was a son of David born in Jerusalem.

eliphelet-2sa-5-16.name: Eliphelet
eliphelet-2sa-5-16.brief: A son of David born in Jerusalem.
eliphelet-2sa-5-16.short: Eliphelet was a son of David born to him in Jerusalem.

samuel-1sa-1-20.name: Samuel
samuel-1sa-1-20.brief: Prophet and last judge of Israel before the kings
samuel-1sa-1-20.short: Samuel was a prophet and the last judge of Israel before the establishment of the monarchy, who anointed both Saul and David as kings.
samuel-1sa-1-20.story: The son Hannah asked of the LORD, given to the LORD at Shiloh, who grew up a prophet, judged Israel all his life, and anointed its first two kings.

nathan-2sa-7-2.name: Nathan
nathan-2sa-7-2.brief: Prophet during the reigns of David and Solomon.
nathan-2sa-7-2.short: Nathan, a prophet of God, served during the reigns of David and Solomon, offering guidance, confronting David's sin, and supporting Solomon's accession to the throne.
nathan-2sa-7-2.story: The prophet in David's court who brought God's promise of a lasting house, rebuked David over Bath-sheba, and helped bring Solomon to the throne.

gad-1sa-22-5.name: Gad
gad-1sa-22-5.brief: Prophet during the reigns of David and Solomon.
gad-1sa-22-5.short: Gad was a prophet who advised King David and wrote a book of his acts.
gad-1sa-22-5.story: A prophet called David's seer, who sent David from the hold into Judah, brought the LORD's three choices after the census, and named the place for an altar.

uriah-2sa-11-3.name: Uriah
uriah-2sa-11-3.short: Uriah was a Hittite soldier in David's army, the husband of Bathsheba, who was killed in battle as part of David's plan to cover up his adultery with Bathsheba.

zadok-2sa-8-17.name: Zadok
zadok-2sa-8-17.brief: High priest during the reigns of David and Solomon
zadok-2sa-8-17.short: Zadok was a prominent high priest who served during the reigns of King David and King Solomon.
zadok-2sa-8-17.story: The son of Ahitub, priest with Abiathar in David's days, who stayed loyal through Absalom's revolt, anointed Solomon king, and took Abiathar's place.

benaiah-2sa-8-18.name: Benaiah
benaiah-2sa-8-18.brief: Son of Jehoiada, a mighty warrior and loyal supporter of David and Solomon.
benaiah-2sa-8-18.short: Benaiah, the son of Jehoiada, was a mighty warrior in David's army and later served as the commander of Solomon's army and a key advisor to the king.

abiathar-1sa-22-20.name: Abiathar
abiathar-1sa-22-20.brief: High priest during the reigns of David and Solomon
abiathar-1sa-22-20.short: Abiathar, son of Ahimelech, was a high priest who served during the reigns of David and Solomon.
abiathar-1sa-22-20.story: The son of Ahimelech who escaped Saul's slaughter of the priests at Nob, served David with the ephod, and was sent home to Anathoth by Solomon.

caption.text: Now the sons of Saul were Jonathan, and Ishui, and Melchi-shua: and the names of his two daughters were these; the name of the firstborn Merab, and the name of the younger Michal: And the name of Saul’s wife was Ahinoam, the daughter of Ahimaaz: and the name of the captain of his host was Abner, the son of Ner, Saul’s uncle. And Kish was the father of Saul; and Ner the father of Abner was the son of Abiel.
And Obed begat Jesse, and Jesse begat David.

And Jesse begat his firstborn Eliab, and Abinadab the second, and Shimma the third, Nethaneel the fourth, Raddai the fifth, Ozem the sixth, David the seventh: Whose sisters were Zeruiah, and Abigail. And the sons of Zeruiah; Abishai, and Joab, and Asahel, three.
Samuel anointed David, Jesse's youngest son, at Bethlehem “in the midst of his brethren”, while Saul still reigned.
Then Samuel took the horn of oil, and anointed him in the midst of his brethren: and the Spirit of the LORD came upon David from that day forward. So Samuel rose up, and went to Ramah.

And it came to pass, when he had made an end of speaking unto Saul, that the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul. And Saul took him that day, and would let him go no more home to his father’s house. Then Jonathan and David made a covenant, because he loved him as his own soul.
But it came to pass at the time when Merab Saul’s daughter should have been given to David, that she was given unto Adriel the Meholathite to wife.

Wherefore David arose and went, he and his men, and slew of the Philistines two hundred men; and David brought their foreskins, and they gave them in full tale to the king, that he might be the king’s son in law. And Saul gave him Michal his daughter to wife.

And Abigail hasted, and arose, and rode upon an ass, with five damsels of hers that went after her; and she went after the messengers of David, and became his wife. David also took Ahinoam of Jezreel; and they were also both of them his wives.
But Saul had given Michal his daughter, David’s wife, to Phalti the son of Laish, which was of Gallim.
The Philistines beat Israel on mount Gilboa. Jonathan, Abinadab and Malchi-shua were killed, and Saul fell on his sword.
And the Philistines followed hard upon Saul and upon his sons; and the Philistines slew Jonathan, and Abinadab, and Malchi-shua, Saul’s sons.
So Saul died, and his three sons, and his armourbearer, and all his men, that same day together.
“there they anointed David king over the house of Judah.”
After Saul's death David asked the LORD where to go, went up to Hebron, and “the men of Judah came, and there they anointed David king over the house of Judah”.

But Abner the son of Ner, captain of Saul’s host, took Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, and brought him over to Mahanaim; And made him king over Gilead, and over the Ashurites, and over Jezreel, and over Ephraim, and over Benjamin, and over all Israel. Ish-bosheth Saul’s son was forty years old when he began to reign over Israel, and reigned two years. But the house of Judah followed David.

caption.event: War with the house of Saul
caption.text: Joab beat Abner at the pool of Gibeon, and the long war followed.

Howbeit he refused to turn aside: wherefore Abner with the hinder end of the spear smote him under the fifth rib, that the spear came out behind him; and he fell down there, and died in the same place: and it came to pass, that as many as came to the place where Asahel fell down and died stood still.
Now there was long war between the house of Saul and the house of David: but David waxed stronger and stronger, and the house of Saul waxed weaker and weaker.

And it came to pass, while there was war between the house of Saul and the house of David, that Abner made himself strong for the house of Saul. And Saul had a concubine, whose name was Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah: and Ish-bosheth said to Abner, Wherefore hast thou gone in unto my father’s concubine?

And unto David were sons born in Hebron: and his firstborn was Amnon, of Ahinoam the Jezreelitess; And his second, Chileab, of Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite; and the third, Absalom the son of Maacah the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur; And the fourth, Adonijah the son of Haggith; and the fifth, Shephatiah the son of Abital; And the sixth, Ithream, by Eglah David’s wife. These were born to David in Hebron.

And David sent messengers to Ish-bosheth Saul’s son, saying, Deliver me my wife Michal, which I espoused to me for an hundred foreskins of the Philistines. And Ish-bosheth sent, and took her from her husband, even from Phaltiel the son of Laish. And her husband went with her along weeping behind her to Bahurim. Then said Abner unto him, Go, return. And he returned.
And when Abner was returned to Hebron, Joab took him aside in the gate to speak with him quietly, and smote him there under the fifth rib, that he died, for the blood of Asahel his brother.
Rechab and Baanah killed him at noon and carried his head to Hebron.

And Jonathan, Saul’s son, had a son that was lame of his feet. He was five years old when the tidings came of Saul and Jonathan out of Jezreel, and his nurse took him up, and fled: and it came to pass, as she made haste to flee, that he fell, and became lame. And his name was Mephibosheth.
The elders of Israel anointed him king over Israel at Hebron after seven years and six months there.
After Abner and Ish-bosheth were dead, the tribes came to Hebron; David “made a league with them”, and “they anointed David king over Israel”.

David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years. In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months: and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty and three years over all Israel and Judah.
David took “the strong hold of Zion”, lived in the fort, called it “the city of David”, and built round about from Millo.

steps.title: Wives and sons in Jerusalem
covers: Philistines beaten in the valley of Rephaim

caption.text: And David took him more concubines and wives out of Jerusalem, after he was come from Hebron: and there were yet sons and daughters born to David. And these be the names of those that were born unto him in Jerusalem; Shammua, and Shobab, and Nathan, and Solomon, Ibhar also, and Elishua, and Nepheg, and Japhia, And Elishama, and Eliada, and Eliphalet.
The tree hangs the four on Bath-sheba because 1 Chronicles 3:5 gives them to her; 2 Samuel 5:14 lists them without a mother.
David brought the ark into the city of David with sacrifices, dancing “with all his might”, and set it in the tent he had pitched. Michal despised him.
Therefore Michal the daughter of Saul had no child unto the day of her death.
David wanted to build a house for the ark. Through Nathan the LORD said that David's son would build it, and that David's house, kingdom and throne would be “established for ever”.
And thine house and thy kingdom shall be established for ever before thee: thy throne shall be established for ever.
David took Metheg-ammah from the Philistines and made Moab his servants, bringing gifts.
David struck Hadadezer of Zobah “as he went to recover his border at the river Euphrates”, killed 22,000 Syrians of Damascus who came to help, and put garrisons in Damascus.
For Jonathan's sake David restored Saul's land to Jonathan's lame son and had him eat at the king's table.
So Mephibosheth dwelt in Jerusalem: for he did eat continually at the king’s table; and was lame on both his feet.
Hanun of Ammon shamed David's messengers and hired Syrians. Joab and Abishai beat both, and David beat Hadarezer's Syrians at Helam.

While Joab besieged Rabbah, David lay with Bathsheba, Uriah's wife, then had Uriah put “in the forefront of the hottest battle”, where he was killed. “But the thing that David had done displeased the LORD.”
And David sent and enquired after the woman. And one said, Is not this Bath-sheba, the daughter of Eliam, the wife of Uriah the Hittite?
And the men of the city went out, and fought with Joab: and there fell some of the people of the servants of David; and Uriah the Hittite died also.
And when the mourning was past, David sent and fetched her to his house, and she became his wife, and bare him a son. But the thing that David had done displeased the LORD.
Nathan's parable of the ewe lamb, the LORD's sentence, and David's confession. The child died.

And it came to pass on the seventh day, that the child died. And the servants of David feared to tell him that the child was dead: for they said, Behold, while the child was yet alive, we spake unto him, and he would not hearken unto our voice: how will he then vex himself, if we tell him that the child is dead?
Bathsheba bore Solomon; “the LORD loved him”, and Nathan named him Jedidiah.
And David comforted Bath-sheba his wife, and went in unto her, and lay with her: and she bare a son, and he called his name Solomon: and the LORD loved him.
2 Samuel narrates Solomon's birth; the other three sons Chronicles gives to Bath-shua are listed, not narrated.
Amnon forced his half-sister Tamar. Two years later Absalom had him killed and fled to Geshur for three years.
And it came to pass after this, that Absalom the son of David had a fair sister, whose name was Tamar; and Amnon the son of David loved her.

interval.quote: And it came to pass after two full years, that Absalom had sheepshearers in Baal-hazor, which is beside Ephraim: and Absalom invited all the king’s sons.

caption.text: And it came to pass after two full years, that Absalom had sheepshearers in Baal-hazor, which is beside Ephraim: and Absalom invited all the king’s sons.
And the servants of Absalom did unto Amnon as Absalom had commanded. Then all the king’s sons arose, and every man gat him up upon his mule, and fled.

interval.quote: So Absalom fled, and went to Geshur, and was there three years.

caption.text: So Absalom fled, and went to Geshur, and was there three years.

steps.title: Back, but not before the king

interval.quote: So Absalom dwelt two full years in Jerusalem, and saw not the king’s face.

caption.text: So Absalom dwelt two full years in Jerusalem, and saw not the king’s face.

interval.question: david-absalom-forty
interval.quote: And it came to pass after forty years, that Absalom said unto the king, I pray thee, let me go and pay my vow, which I have vowed unto the LORD, in Hebron.

caption.text: Absalom “stole the hearts of the men of Israel”, had himself proclaimed king in Hebron, and drew Ahithophel to his side.
But Absalom sent spies throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, As soon as ye hear the sound of the trumpet, then ye shall say, Absalom reigneth in Hebron.

And Absalom made Amasa captain of the host instead of Joab: which Amasa was a man’s son, whose name was Ithra an Israelite, that went in to Abigail the daughter of Nahash, sister to Zeruiah Joab’s mother.

steps.title: Flight over the mount of Olives

caption.event: Flight over the mount of Olives
caption.text: David left Jerusalem and went up the ascent of the mount of Olives weeping, barefoot. At Bahurim Shimei cursed him.
David's men beat Israel in the wood of Ephraim. Absalom was caught by his head in an oak, and Joab killed him. David wept: “O my son Absalom”.
Then said Joab, I may not tarry thus with thee. And he took three darts in his hand, and thrust them through the heart of Absalom, while he was yet alive in the midst of the oak.

And the king was much moved, and went up to the chamber over the gate, and wept: and as he went, thus he said, O my son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom! would God I had died for thee, O Absalom, my son, my son!

caption.event: Return, and Judah and Israel quarrel
caption.text: Judah brought the king back over the Jordan; the men of Israel complained that Judah had “stolen thee away”.
And say ye to Amasa, Art thou not of my bone, and of my flesh? God do so to me, and more also, if thou be not captain of the host before me continually in the room of Joab.

Sheba blew a trumpet: “We have no part in David”. Israel followed him; Judah stayed with David. Joab killed Amasa, besieged Sheba in Abel of Beth-maachah, and the city threw Sheba's head over the wall.

But Amasa took no heed to the sword that was in Joab’s hand: so he smote him therewith in the fifth rib, and shed out his bowels to the ground, and struck him not again; and he died. So Joab and Abishai his brother pursued after Sheba the son of Bichri.

Three years of famine were laid to Saul's killing of Gibeonites. David handed seven of Saul's descendants to the Gibeonites, spared Mephibosheth, and buried Saul's and Jonathan's bones in Kish's tomb.

But the king spared Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan the son of Saul, because of the LORD’s oath that was between them, between David and Jonathan the son of Saul. But the king took the two sons of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, whom she bare unto Saul, Armoni and Mephibosheth; and the five sons of Michal the daughter of Saul, whom she brought up for Adriel the son of Barzillai the Meholathite: And he delivered them into the hands of the Gibeonites, and they hanged them in the hill before the LORD: and they fell all seven together, and were put to death in the days of harvest, in the first days, in the beginning of barley harvest.
In four battles David's men killed four men “born to the giant in Gath”. David “waxed faint”, and his men swore he would go out to battle no more.
David's song of deliverance, and the “last words” of “the sweet psalmist of Israel”.
David had Joab number Israel and Judah; it took nine months and twenty days.
At Gad's word David bought the threshingfloor and built an altar, “and the plague was stayed from Israel”. Chronicles adds that David said, “This is the house of the LORD God”.
Chronicles alone tells how David gathered gold, silver, brass, iron, timber and stone, ordered the Levites, priests, singers and gatekeepers, and gave Solomon the pattern of the house.
When David was old, Adonijah declared himself king. At Nathan's and Bathsheba's urging David had Solomon anointed at Gihon.
David charged Solomon to keep the LORD's ways, and died.

So David slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David. And the days that David reigned over Israel were forty years: seven years reigned he in Hebron, and thirty and three years reigned he in Jerusalem.

Now therefore, as the LORD liveth, which hath established me, and set me on the throne of David my father, and who hath made me an house, as he promised, Adonijah shall be put to death this day. And king Solomon sent by the hand of Benaiah the son of Jehoiada; and he fell upon him that he died.
Then tidings came to Joab: for Joab had turned after Adonijah, though he turned not after Absalom. And Joab fled unto the tabernacle of the LORD, and caught hold on the horns of the altar.
So Benaiah the son of Jehoiada went up, and fell upon him, and slew him: and he was buried in his own house in the wilderness.
Now king David was old and stricken in years; and they covered him with clothes, but he gat no heat.
Then Adonijah the son of Haggith exalted himself, saying, I will be king: and he prepared him chariots and horsemen, and fifty men to run before him.
And he conferred with Joab the son of Zeruiah, and with Abiathar the priest: and they following Adonijah helped him.
But Zadok the priest, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and Nathan the prophet, and Shimei, and Rei, and the mighty men which belonged to David, were not with Adonijah.
But Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah, and the mighty men, and Solomon his brother, he called not.

Wherefore Nathan spake unto Bath-sheba the mother of Solomon, saying, Hast thou not heard that Adonijah the son of Haggith doth reign, and David our lord knoweth it not? Now therefore come, let me, I pray thee, give thee counsel, that thou mayest save thine own life, and the life of thy son Solomon. Go and get thee in unto king David, and say unto him, Didst not thou, my lord, O king, swear unto thine handmaid, saying, Assuredly Solomon thy son shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my throne? why then doth Adonijah reign?

drama.title: Bath-sheba goes in to the king

caption.text: And Bath-sheba went in unto the king into the chamber: and the king was very old; and Abishag the Shunammite ministered unto the king. And Bath-sheba bowed, and did obeisance unto the king. And the king said, What wouldest thou? And she said unto him, My lord, thou swarest by the LORD thy God unto thine handmaid, saying, Assuredly Solomon thy son shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my throne. And now, behold, Adonijah reigneth; and now, my lord the king, thou knowest it not:

And, lo, while she yet talked with the king, Nathan the prophet also came in. And they told the king, saying, Behold Nathan the prophet. And when he was come in before the king, he bowed himself before the king with his face to the ground. And Nathan said, My lord, O king, hast thou said, Adonijah shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my throne?

And the king sware, and said, As the LORD liveth, that hath redeemed my soul out of all distress, Even as I sware unto thee by the LORD God of Israel, saying, Assuredly Solomon thy son shall reign after me, and he shall sit upon my throne in my stead; even so will I certainly do this day.

So Zadok the priest, and Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites, and the Pelethites, went down, and caused Solomon to ride upon king David’s mule, and brought him to Gihon. And Zadok the priest took an horn of oil out of the tabernacle, and anointed Solomon. And they blew the trumpet; and all the people said, God save king Solomon.

And all the guests that were with Adonijah were afraid, and rose up, and went every man his way. And Adonijah feared because of Solomon, and arose, and went, and caught hold on the horns of the altar.

verses.text: Now David was the son of that Ephrathite of Beth-lehem-judah, whose name was Jesse; and he had eight sons: and the man went among men for an old man in the days of Saul.

And unto David were sons born in Hebron: and his firstborn was Amnon, of Ahinoam the Jezreelitess; And his second, Chileab, of Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite; and the third, Absalom the son of Maacah the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur; And the fourth, Adonijah the son of Haggith; and the fifth, Shephatiah the son of Abital; And the sixth, Ithream, by Eglah David’s wife. These were born to David in Hebron.

And these be the names of those that were born unto him in Jerusalem; Shammua, and Shobab, and Nathan, and Solomon, Ibhar also, and Elishua, and Nepheg, and Japhia, And Elishama, and Eliada, and Eliphalet.
And Jesse begat his firstborn Eliab, and Abinadab the second, and Shimma the third, Nethaneel the fourth, Raddai the fifth, Ozem the sixth, David the seventh:

Now these were the sons of David, which were born unto him in Hebron; the firstborn Amnon, of Ahinoam the Jezreelitess; the second Daniel, of Abigail the Carmelitess: The third, Absalom the son of Maachah the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur: the fourth, Adonijah the son of Haggith: The fifth, Shephatiah of Abital: the sixth, Ithream by Eglah his wife. These six were born unto him in Hebron; and there he reigned seven years and six months: and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty and three years. And these were born unto him in Jerusalem; Shimea, and Shobab, and Nathan, and Solomon, four, of Bath-shua the daughter of Ammiel: Ibhar also, and Elishama, and Eliphelet, And Nogah, and Nepheg, and Japhia, And Elishama, and Eliada, and Eliphelet, nine. These were all the sons of David, beside the sons of the concubines, and Tamar their sister.
